ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the hexagon $ABCDEF$, if $\angle 1 + \angle 2 + \angle 3 = 140^\circ$, then $\angle 4 + \angle 5 + \angle 6 = ?$ degrees.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the sum of the exterior angles of any polygon equals $360^\circ$, we have $\angle 1+\angle 2+\angle 3+\angle 4+\angle 5+\angle 6=360^\circ$,\\
since $\angle 1+\angle 2+\angle 3=140^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle 4+\angle 5+\angle 6=360^\circ-140^\circ=\boxed{220^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: From the diagram, pair each labeled exterior angle with the corresponding interior angle of hexagon ABCDEF at the same vertex. Each exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a linear pair, so their sums are 180°. Let the six interior angles be A_i through F_i. Then (angle 1+...+angle 6)+(sum of six interior angles)=6×180°. For a hexagon, the interior-angle sum is (6-2)×180°=720°. Hence angle 1+...+angle 6=1080°-720°=360°. Since the text states angle 1+angle 2+angle 3=140°, subtract to get angle 4+angle 5+angle 6=220°.
